title: Metric pruning simulation & trace sampling playground
content:
Purpose

Quick playground notes for simulating the impact of metric pruning and adaptive trace sampling on dashboard signal fidelity and query cost. Primary goal: produce an experiment matrix we can run in the telemetry sandbox and a short checklist for what to validate before making pruning changes live.

Background / motivation

We have a growing panel of high-cardinality metrics and expensive dashboard queries (tokenized inference + KV cache joins). Query costs and dashboard flakiness are increasing—esp. for tenant heatmaps and per-model latency rollups. Rather than ad hoc pruning, run controlled sims to estimate:
- SLI fidelity loss for different pruning sets
- Trace-capture coverage versus cost for severity-weighted sampling
- Query cost reduction for dashboard types (operator, executive, tenant)

Hypotheses to test

1) Removing the bottom 20% of metric time-series (by traffic and alert-rate correlation) reduces dashboard query cost by ~25% with <1% SLI degradation.
2) Severity-weighted adaptive sampling (p50/p90/p99-driven) yields 40–60% fewer traces stored while preserving root-cause signal for top-5 incident classes.
3) Lightweight synthetic rollups (store pre-aggregated quintiles for cold/rare tenants) reduces per-query CPU by 30% with acceptable latency for operator workflows.

Experiment matrix (playground runs)

Rows: pruning tiers A/B/C (conservative/moderate/aggressive) + sampling policy X/Y/Z (uniform, severity-weighted, dynamic window). Columns: SLI set (latency, error_rate, cold_cache_rate), storage cost, dashboard query time, investigation success rate (simulated).

Quick plan steps

1) Select candidate metrics: run correlation analysis over 90d to find low-utility series (low variance, low-alert-correlation, high-cardinality but low-owner). Output list and owner recommendations.
2) Create synthetic query load using existing dashboard SQL + replayed access patterns for last 30d.
3) Apply pruning tiers to telemetry snapshot (sandbox index) and re-run query load. Collect query wall-time, CPU, and cost per-query.
4) Enable sampling policy in sandbox collector for same period; measure traces saved, average spans per trace, percentage of incident traces preserved (compare to full capture baseline).
5) Run investigator vignettes: give human operator a set of 10 seeded incidents in the sandbox dashboards and measure time-to-first-hypothesis & success (qualitative).

Metric pruning heuristics (initial rules)

- Keep: metrics tied to SLIs, product-facing quotas, billing, security-sensitive indicators.
- Candidate prune: derived metrics not linked to owned SLOs, high-cardinality labels with sparsity >90%, metrics that duplicate rollups available elsewhere.
- Defer: unowned metrics or metrics without documented consumers for >120 days.

Sampling policies to benchmark

- Uniform-1/N: deterministic sample 1 in N traces. Pros: simple. Cons: misses rare failures.
- Severity-weighted: sample more aggressively when latency/error anomalies detected (p99 spike, nonzero error rate). Tunables: base-rate, multiplier for severity buckets.
- Dynamic-window: keep full traces for a sliding window around anomalies (e.g., 30s before/5m after threshold crossing), otherwise low-rate sampling.

Key metrics to collect for each experiment

- Dashboard query median and p95 latency (ms)
- Aggregate query cost ($ / 10k queries)
- Stored metric volume (GB/day) and cardinality delta
- Traces stored per day and avg spans per trace
- Investigation success fraction (operator-run vignettes)
- False-negative rate for incident detection (alerts that lose signal post-prune)

Dashboard scaffold notes (what to build for the sandbox)

- Cost dashboard: query-type breakdown, cost per-panel, cost trend after pruning
- Fidelity dashboard: compare baseline vs pruned SLI curves (overlay), show confidence intervals
- Trace coverage panel: traces/day, severity distribution, capture ratio by tenant
- Investigator quickcard: for seeded incidents show top-3 root-cause signals (pre/post prune)

Acceptance criteria to promote a pruning/sampling config

- No SLI regression > 0.5% absolute on production SLOs across 30d synthetic runs
- Alert recall >= 98% for top-10 alert classes in sandbox vignettes
- Dashboard query cost reduction >= 20% for operator panels, >=10% for exec panels
- Owner sign-off (metric owners listed) or automatic archival with owner contact created

Open questions / decisions

- Retention tiers: if we prune a metric, should we keep 7d high-res then tumble to 1d aggregates for 90d? (tradeoff: rehydration complexity vs query cost)
- Ownerless metrics: auto-delete after X days or auto-request owner via batched Slack message?
- Sampling instrumentation: can we add a lightweight trace index for keywords (error codes, tenant id) so we can still search without full traces?

Next actionable tasks (owner + ETA)

- Asha: produce correlation export and initial candidate list (ETA: 2024-11-20)
- Miguel: build sandbox replay harness + synthetic incidents (ETA: 2024-11-28)
- Samira: prototype severity-weighted sampler in collector (ETA: 2024-12-05)
- Liam: dashboard scaffolding and cost-calculator panels (ETA: 2024-12-08)

Notes-to-self / rough command snippets

- sample SQL to compute metric variance and owner coverage:
  SELECT metric_name, approx_count_distinct(labels) as card, stddev(value) as sd, count(*) as points, max(last_seen) as last_seen, owner
  FROM telemetry.metrics_snap
  WHERE ts >= now() - interval '90 days'
  GROUP BY metric_name, owner
  ORDER BY sd asc, points asc

- rough cost estimate formula: (query_seconds * cpu_rate) + (storage_gb * storage_rate) + (ingest_events * ingest_rate)

If you want to run an ad-hoc sim with me, ping in #eng-observability and drop the dataset id (sandbox-tv-2024-11).

End of doc.
